messages:
maria: Heads-up — multiple customers started seeing 502s from the edge gateway ~09:40 UTC during a burst of embed requests. Getting consistent proxy 502s (no 5xx body) with trace ids in the logs. Example response headers from a failing call:

maria: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  --data '{"model":"embed-xl","input":"short text"}' 

< HTTP/2 502
< date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:41:02 GMT
< server: nginx/1.21.6
< x-redwood-trace: c3f2a9e7
< content-length: 0
```

maria: Observed these from EU1 and us-west, spike coincides with a batch job from tenant `acme-inc` (100 concurrent small-embed requests).

sre-bot: Alert: edge.gateway.502_rate high in prod-eu1 (link: https://alerts.redwood.ai/alerts/EDGE-502-spike-2150009999) :rotating_light:

ankit: @maria thanks. Can you paste a few trace IDs and a snippet of the edge proxy logs around one? Also curious if we see upstream resets or h2 window errors. Quick checks: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9901/stats?filter=upstream_rq_5xx` and `grep -E \"upstream_reset|h2_window\" /var/log/edge/proxy.log | tail -n 50`

maria: Trace ids: c3f2a9e7, f8b1d2c4, 9a7c3e11. I pulled a tiny excerpt: 

maria: ```
2026-03-18T09:41:02Z edge-proxy[pid]: trace=c3f2a9e7 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=502 upstream=envoy_upstream reset=none auth_status=MISS
2026-03-18T09:41:02Z edge-proxy[pid]: trace=f8b1d2c4 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=502 upstream=envoy_upstream reset=CONNECT_FAILURE auth_status=MISS
```

maria: We also see a lot of `auth_status=MISS` in the same window.

julian: Can customer reproduce? Need a minimal repro curl (http2). If we can repro, we can attach an envoy /admin log. Try: `curl --http2 -v -X POST https://...` with same body.

lisa: My hunch: auth-cache eviction + sudden fanout causes upstream queue/backpressure and envoy returns 502 when midproxy can't accept streams. If the auth tier is suddenly cold for that tenant, we get a thundering herd. Two quick things to check: auth-cache miss rate and midproxy socket/buffer stats. E.g.: 

lisa: ```
# auth cache misses in last 200 lines
tail -n 200 /var/log/edge/auth-cache.log | grep -c \"MISS\"

# envoy upstream resets/stats
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9901/stats?filter=cluster\.edge_midproxy
```

lisa: Also grep for `upstream_cx_overflow` and `upstream_rq_pending_overflow` — we've hit these before with small-concurrency bursts.

ankit: If that's true, immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily cap concurrent embeds per-tenant via rate limit rule; 2) scale midproxy pool or increase connections; 3) enable short warmup for `acme-inc` (pin to warm pool). Which can you do quickly @maria?

maria: I just pushed a tenant-level concurrency cap in the console (limit 20 concurrent) and throttled the worst customer for 10m. Error rate dropped from ~8% -> ~1% in 6 minutes. :thumbsup:

julian: Nice. Can you capture full envoy /admin dump for one failing trace and attach to the support ticket? We need `GET /clusters` and `GET /stats?format=prometheus` around the time.

maria: Will attach. Uploading logs/trace c3f2a9e7 to ticket #T-8421 now.

lisa: Follow-up: we should add an auth-cache warmup to the onboarding path and add a runbook entry for multi-tenant embed bursts (runbook: warm auth cache + scale midproxy + fallback to dedicated auth endpoint). I can open a small PR to change TTL and add the runbook.

ankit: Agreed — will schedule a short canary for the TTL bump and watch `edge.gateway.502_rate` and `upstream_rq_pending_overflow`.

maria: Thanks everyone — customers are updated that we applied temporary throttle while we validate the fix.
